request: Independently critique and improve one *minimal, executable* finite-state reconciliation model for external AI/model dispatch of uncertain outcome. We want a public-safe research artifact, not a deployed runner. Name the smallest state and evidence needed; specify safety and useful-availability properties, competing algorithms/mutants that an independent checker should catch, and one minimal counterexample. Keep answer under 650 words. Do not assert a provider cause or promise at-most-once external calls.
context: Continuum public development: Rust/SQLite native core currently has exact bytes, local operation identity binding, accepted-head generation, historical receipt retry. It has no external model dispatcher, authenticated receiver or remote effects. The public design requires an explicit dispatch reconciliation protocol before remote runner adoption. GitHub is a separate durability/coordination host. A model call can end with a transport result such as invalid_response, inference_outcome unknown and upstream HTTP200 without an accepted usable reply. Do not blindly replay unknown calls. Known pre-send validation rejection is different from send/unknown. We intend to build a separate, standalone pure Python bounded model/oracle on synthetic data with no SDK, network or actual inference. It must separate submitted requests, external effects, observed authoritative receipts, locally offered/historical work, and model output acceptance. We would leave production Rust/SQLite code unchanged. Existing assistant tests and current real-use pilots are observational, not general reliability claims. Cross-repo private data and code must remain private.
